headline: Mistakes to Avoid During a Whole-House Renovation
articleBody:
Renovating an entire home requires careful coordination. When homeowners jump in without a structured plan, small oversights can lead to major budget overruns. Here are typical pitfalls and how to avoid them:

- Treating the project as disconnected rooms: Remodeling room by room without a master plan leads to mismatched flooring heights, inconsistent trim, and redundant plumbing runs. Design your home as a single unified system.
- Ignoring aging utility systems: Installing luxury kitchen cabinets over fifty-year-old galvanized pipes or ungrounded wiring invites future leaks and hazards. Address infrastructure before finishes.
- Delaying appliance and fixture selections: Failing to provide exact appliance specifications early leaves cabinet makers and electricians guessing on rough openings and dedicated circuit locations.
- Underestimating site protection and temporary storage: Leaving furniture on-site or failing to seal HVAC returns fills vents and upholstery with fine construction dust. Plan for off-site storage.
- Failing to verify licensing and insurance: Hiring unvetted labor without verifying state contractor licensing exposes you to liability and uninspected work.
